name: RWANDA

flag.title: Flag of Rwanda
flag.note: Blue, yellow & green with a gold sun

lead: Rwanda is a small country in the middle of Africa. It has no coast. Green hills fill the land, so it is called the Land of a Thousand Hills. A terrible tragedy struck in 1994. Today Rwanda is one of Africa's cleanest, safest countries.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Rwanda sits high up. Even its lowest valleys are about 1,000 m above sea level. Ridge after ridge of green hills crumples the land.
Volcanoes rise in the north, wrapped in misty forest. Lake Kivu shines on the western border. Nyungwe Forest, in the south, is one of Africa's oldest rainforests.
animals: The mountain gorilla is Rwanda's star. Fewer than 1,000 survive in the wild. Rwanda protects about a third of them.
Chimpanzees and black-and-white colobus monkeys leap through Nyungwe Forest. Over 700 kinds of birds have been seen in Rwanda.
culture: Every August, Rwandans celebrate Umuganura, a harvest festival. In the intore dance, warriors leap in headdresses of white plant fibres that stream like waterfalls.
Rwandans weave coiled peace baskets called agaseke. On the last Saturday of each month, everyone sweeps streets and plants trees. This is Umuganda, community work day.
history: For centuries a king called the mwami ruled Rwanda. His kingdom had an organised army and many cattle. Later, rulers from Belgium divided people into groups.
In 1994, around 800,000 people were killed in 100 days. Afterwards, Rwandans chose peace. Community courts called gacaca heard over a million cases.
wows: Over 60% of Rwanda's parliament is female, the world's highest share.
Kigali, the capital, rated Africa's cleanest city, has banned plastic bags since 2008.
A single gorilla trek permit costs 1,500 USD, and gorillas are Rwanda's top tourist earner.
No road in Rwanda stays straight for more than about 30 km, because the hills never stop.
Once a month, everyone does community work, even the president.
Rwanda pipes up methane, a burnable gas, hidden in Lake Kivu's water to make electricity.
Rwanda has no sea, yet its national sailing team competes internationally.

myths.fact: Mountain gorillas eat plants, mostly leaves and stems. A big male eats about 18 kg a day.

myths.myth: Gorillas beat their chests to attack
myths.fact: Chest-beating is mostly a show. Males use it to warn rivals, and real fights are rare.
